fish.name: Cavern Chub
fish.flavor: The bread-and-butter catch of the underlake. Tastes faintly of rainwater and patience.

fish.name: Pebble Gudgeon
fish.flavor: Indistinguishable from gravel until it panics. It panics often.

fish.name: Milkfin Darter
fish.flavor: Its fins are the soft white of a mushroom cap. Locals swear eating one before bed guarantees dull, restful dreams, which is exactly what they want.

fish.name: Dripstone Dace
fish.flavor: Sits beneath the stalactites and lets the drips bonk it on the head, apparently on purpose. Scholars call the behavior 'inexplicable.' Locals call it 'Tuesday.'

fish.name: Chalk Roach
fish.flavor: Pale as a fresh page and about as exciting, which around here counts as dependable.

fish.name: Tallow Sculpin
fish.flavor: Greasy to the touch and unbothered by criticism. Old-timers claim you can render a candle from three of them; nobody has needed to test this in generations.

fish.name: Glowworm Fry
fish.flavor: Gathers beneath the glowworm ceilings with its mouth open, hoping. The worms remain unimpressed and firmly attached.

fish.name: Cellar Smelt
fish.flavor: Smells like a grandmother's root cellar: cool, earthy, and vaguely disapproving.

fish.name: Mosspocket Carp
fish.flavor: Carries a soft green fuzz on its scales. Cavern kids race them in the shallows; the moss makes them easy to tell apart and equally easy to lose.

fish.name: Rubble Bullhead
fish.flavor: Wedges itself into old rockfalls and dares you to do something about it. The bait usually does.

fish.name: Echo Minnow
fish.flavor: Schools of them turn as one at every sound. Yodel into the cavern and watch a thousand tiny fish judge you in unison.

fish.name: Blindside Loach
fish.flavor: It has no eyes and no regrets. Navigates by bumping into things with tremendous confidence.

fish.name: Lantern-Keeper's Perch
fish.flavor: Loiters wherever fishers hang their lamps, eating whatever the light lures in. Not lazy — efficient.

fish.name: Coldwick Trout
fish.flavor: A trout that wandered underground three floods ago and decided it preferred the quiet. Honestly, fair.

fish.name: Crystalback Grayling
fish.flavor: Grows a ridge of quartz-like scales along its spine. Jewelers frown at it; the grayling has never once cared.

fish.name: Two-Lantern Catfish
fish.flavor: Its barbels end in two faintly glowing bulbs. It patrols the underlake slow and steady, like a night watchman who knows nothing ever happens.

fish.name: Sootgill Pike
fish.flavor: Its gills are stained dark, though no one has ever found a fire down here. The pike declines to comment.

fish.name: Whistlefin Char
fish.flavor: Its dorsal fin whistles softly when it swims fast. A school of them in a hurry sounds like a kettle reaching consensus.

fish.name: Quartzjaw Barbel
fish.flavor: Its teeth glint like crystal chips. Bites through lines, hooks, and the occasional cherished belief that you'd finally caught it.

fish.name: Stalactite Sniffer
fish.flavor: Noses along the ceiling drip-lines, sipping mineral water like a connoisseur. Frankly, it has better taste than most tavern patrons.

fish.name: Drip-Counter Loach
fish.flavor: Locals swear it can count. It stations itself beneath a stalactite and flinches exactly once per drip, forever.

fish.name: Palefire Tetra
fish.flavor: Glows the color of a candle behind a curtain. A jarful of them was this cavern's first streetlight.

fish.name: Gloamshell Snapper
fish.flavor: Wears a crust of tiny cave snails like medals. Nobody knows if the snails agreed to this arrangement, least of all the snails.

fish.name: Silverseam Char
fish.flavor: Its flank carries a bright vein like ore in stone. Miners once followed a school of them to the richest silver lode in the isles — then the school flooded it, which felt fair.

fish.name: Bellringer Bream
fish.flavor: On still nights its tail slaps the water in slow, even tolls. The old ferry crews set their watches by it, which explains a great deal about the old ferry crews.

fish.name: Grotto Ghostfin
fish.flavor: Translucent enough to read a letter through, if you had a letter, and a very patient fish. It watches you back with polite curiosity.

fish.name: Wishing-Well Koi
fish.flavor: Escaped a surface wishing well generations ago and swam deep, scales still studded with old coins. It grants no wishes, but it kept every one it heard.

fish.name: Foreman's Lantern
fish.flavor: Carries a steady amber light that never gutters. Old miners say that when a lamp went out down here, something kindly lit one for the walk home.

fish.name: Choir Eel
fish.flavor: Hums low, patient rounds through the flooded galleries, and other eels take up the harmony a tunnel away. Midwinter, the whole underlake sings; the taverns close early so everyone can go listen.

fish.name: The Miner's Widow
fish.flavor: A jet-black fish trailing fins like mourning lace, it circles the drowned cave-ins slowly, keeping a vigil older than anyone can name. Fishers who catch one always let it finish its lap first.

fish.name: Candlesnuffer
fish.flavor: Where it swims, the glowworms hold their breath and the crystals go dim, one by one, like lamps along an emptying street. It isn't hostile. It just prefers not to be looked at.

fish.name: Gallery Hush
fish.flavor: A wide, silent shape that glides beneath your boat like a rumor. The water goes so quiet you can hear your own heartbeat asking to leave.

fish.name: Old Lanternjaw
fish.flavor: Every generation, one fisher swears they hooked it and got towed twice around the underlake before the line sang apart. The tavern buys their supper anyway; some stories are worth the broth.

fish.name: The Glimmermother
fish.flavor: The glowworm ceilings, the old folk say, are her brood hung up to dry. When she rises, the whole cavern brightens like a held breath finally let go.

fish.name: The First Dark
fish.flavor: Older than the glowworms, older than the crystal, older than the word for light. It does not swim through the dark — it is what the dark learned to do.
